data.title: SAP source code target of cyberattack; company says no customer data compromised: report
data.description:
Hackers, possibly using AI-assisted tools, were able to target SAP's (SAP) source code stored on GitHub, according to Der Spiegel, which said the German-based enterprise software firm had confirmed the attack.

Once SAP identified suspicious activity within GitHub, the company immediately took action to mitigate the attack and protect its customers and services, according to the report. The hackers had gained access by acquiring employee authentication tokens, which allowed them to copy and alter source code in GitHub.

"Based on our investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data," SAP said, according to SecurityWeek.

There was also no evidence of tampered code being delivered to SAP's clients. Some of the protective measures included the replacement of signing keys, limited access to GitHub and a suspension of automated development operations.

Seeking Alpha reached out to SAP for comment.

There has been a clear increase in cyberattacks across businesses, government agencies and critical infrastructure. It was reported on Friday that hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform in a development that could jeopardize sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.

data.title: Palantir rises as company signs 5-year, $300M deal with Poland
data.description:
• Palantir (PLTR) shares rose 3% in premarket trading on Friday as the enterprise software giant has signed a five-year deal with Poland worth roughly $300M, the country's defense minister said.
  • The deal will see Palantir provide artificial intelligence-enfused software to help the country's army commanders with their decision-making processes.
  • “We will use (the ​software) to build the best ​possible capabilities. All keys, servers, and information are — ‌and ⁠will remain — the exclusive property of the Polish Armed Forces,” Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said, according to Reuters. Kosiniak-Kamysz added this deal is a “watershed moment” for Poland's armed forces and their capabilities.
  • Earlier this month, Palantir reported third-quarter results that were better-than-expected and upped its full-year guidance, due in part to strong momentum in government contracts.
  • Palantir shares are down 2.5% year-to-date but up more than 670% over the past five years.

data.title: From squishies to can crushers: The toys on the top of Santa's list
data.description:
Forget about an official Red Ryder Carbine-Action 200-shot range model air rifle—the toys kids are waiting to unwrap this holiday season are squishy, loud, and, as always, pricey.

Compiling a list of the most popular toys depends on who you ask. Amazon (AMZN) and Target (TGT) are probably the most popular destinations for kids under 10, while kids 10 and up would most likely prefer their parents shop at Best Buy (BBY) for game consoles, laptops, earbuds, and, of course, the digital download code for Grand Theft Auto VI (TTWO).

Doubling as both collectibles and a calming sensory tool, squishies—including dumpling squishies—are still at the top spot at both Amazon (AMZN) and Target (TGT). The tactile toys are made from slow-rising polyurethane foam that gives a satisfying squeeze and are available in almost unlimited shapes and sizes—from raindrop-shaped squishies to animal-shaped squishies to squishies shaped like a stick of butter.

For creative types, Stickerbox lets kids (and some adults) make their own stickers using AI to generate designs and is equipped with thermal printing that avoids costly ink refills. The $130 Stickerbox is designed to block inappropriate prompts to make sure each sticker is kid-friendly.

Expanding on its "dinosaur hatching" phenomenon from last year, Primal Hatch now allows kids to hatch their own megalodon. Put the egg in the tank, add water, and watch while a shark is “born.” Best part? The color-changing, explosive hatching action can be repeated over and over. Primal Hatch is available at Amazon (AMZN), Walmart (WMT), and Target (TGT) with Amazon (AMZN) offering the best price of $35.

Got a young recycler at home? The Crunchinator and ChompSaw let kids crush empty soda cans and cut up cardboard boxes instead of tossing them.

Designed by a NASA engineer, the $35 Crunchinator enables kids to crush and smash objects in what the company calls “the most satisfyingly destructive ways possible.”

To make use of all those empty Amazon boxes, the $130 Chompshop Chompsaw cuts old cardboard boxes into any shape and any creation to make dioramas, classroom projects, costumes, and whatever else kids can dream up.

For more mindless entertainment, there’s the flying orb ball toy, a “hand-controlled mini drone flight spinner” that can fly, hover, and even respond like a boomerang, all with RGB lighting that creates a mesmerizing light display.

Mattel (MAT) is continuing to cash in on the KPop juggernaut with a new line of KPop Demon Hunters toys, while Disney (DIS) is leaning on a holiday evergreen—a Toy Story figurine line featuring Woody, Jessie, Buzz, Slinky, Rex, and Forky in movie-inspired scale.

Electronics are still a favorite among teens, tweens, and adults with the Consumer Technology Association finding that at least 87% of adults plan to buy tech gifts this holiday season. The most popular for 2026 includes Apple (AAPL) AirPods 5, Sony (SONY) cameras, and Ray-Ban Meta (META) smart glasses, showing that the most-wanted gifts still come with a charging cable.

Target (TGT), Amazon (AMZN), and Best Buy (BBY) all have the Nintendo (NTDOY) Switch 2 Console as one of its bestselling items this holiday season. The next generation of the Nintendo Switch comes with a $500 price tag but gives gamers three play modes: TV, tabletop, and handheld. While the console is compatible with all Nintendo Switch games, it still can’t get you to Vice City.

The toys might change every year—still squishy, still loud, and still pricey—but the mission never does: find the right one before someone else does.

data.title: BofA sets 2027 S&P 500 target at 7,800 after pullback
data.description:
Bank of America Securities this week introduced a 2027 year-end S&P 500 (SP500) target of 7,800, contending that a recent market pullback has created an attractive entry point despite looming earnings deceleration and supply-demand headwinds.

The forecast implies roughly 8.6% upside from Wednesday’s close of 7,182.86—and about 7% from Friday’s implied futures open of 7,290.94—with BofA’s underlying models mapping a wider potential range between 6,600 and 8,500. The index's all-time intraday high is 7,844.52, set in October.

Strategists remain constructive on the back of compressed price-to-earnings multiples and untapped AI-driven productivity gains, noting that higher capital costs and regulatory hurdles should prevent an AI capital expenditure overheat. Reflecting greater value for existing AI (AIQ) (AIEQ) capacity, BofA upgraded communication services (XLC) to Overweight while highlighting stronger conviction in AI adoption through Overweight ratings on financials (XLF) and health care (XLV).

Still, BofA projects S&P 500 earnings-per-share growth to slow sharply from 35% ($370) in 2026 to 14% ($420) in 2027—modestly below the $428 consensus—before normalizing to 7% ($450) in 2028. Because chipmakers (SMH) (SOXX) drive the bulk of profit growth, a 20% cut in AI spending could directly shave 8% off index EPS, compounding broader downside risks from rising equity issuance, waning share buybacks, and potential demographic-driven retirement outflows.

data.title: S&P 500 heads for fourth straight week of outsized moves as volatility persists
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) is on pace to finish the week up roughly 3.9%, extending a stretch of unusually large weekly swings that has now reached four consecutive weeks.

If the current gain holds through the close, the index will have produced moves of at least 2.5% in either direction for a fourth straight week—the longest such run since the 2022 bear market. 

The sequence has been pronounced. Two weeks before last week’s sharp decline, the S&P 500 fell -2.7% and then advanced +2.5%. That rebound was followed by an -8.6% drop last week, one of the steepest weekly losses in recent years, before this week’s recovery. The pattern has kept volatility elevated heading into the end of the trading week.

Historical comparisons underscore how uncommon the streak is. It matches four-week runs recorded during the 2020 sell-off and the decline that followed the Dot-com bust in 2000. The longest comparable stretch on record lasted ten weeks amid the 2008 financial crisis.

While past episodes have often occurred during periods of broader market stress, the present sequence has developed against a backdrop of rapid directional reversals rather than a sustained one-way trend. For participants navigating these conditions, the repeated large weekly moves continue to create an exceptional opportunity to respond to short-term dislocations while monitoring the durability of the current recovery.

data.title: Wall Street rebound faces high bar as earnings risks mount
data.description:
Wall Street’s recent selloff may prove difficult to reverse, with weakening earnings drivers threatening to limit a recovery even as investor risk appetite has fallen sharply, according to TS Lombard.

The research firm said equity markets had come under pressure lately as a more hawkish Federal Reserve and concerns over the profitability of heavy artificial intelligence spending weighed on sentiment. 

A brief improvement following Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO has failed to gain traction, with technology stocks facing another round of selling.

TS Lombard said the recent deterioration in risk appetite appeared excessive but argued that the economic backdrop for corporate earnings had become less supportive. Its risk appetite indicator had fallen to -62.6, while the Global Cross Asset Risk Sentiment Index stood at 38.5.

The firm also noted that the recent reduction in investor positioning had been more moderate than during the 2022 downturn, suggesting markets could struggle to recover their losses before year-end.

The firm identified several headwinds for U.S. corporate earnings. Fiscal policy is expected to weigh on economic growth next year, while growth in hyperscaler capital expenditure, a key driver of corporate profits, appears to have peaked.

TS Lombard also warned that a tightening U.S. labor market could push wage growth higher next year, putting further pressure on corporate profitability.

The firm added that the dollar’s recent appreciation could lead to stronger negative earnings revisions in the U.S., creating another obstacle for equities. Its charts show hyperscaler capex growth on a 12-month forward basis turning lower from its recent peak, while indicators of U.S. hiring and wage growth point to a labor market that could put renewed pressure on costs.

The combination leaves a high bar for a swift market rebound, TS Lombard said. While the selloff has reflected a sharp deterioration in sentiment, the underlying drivers of earnings have also weakened, making it harder for stocks to regain lost ground quickly.

The firm said equities could struggle to recover their recent losses this year, despite the possibility that risk appetite has fallen too far.

data.title: HSBC: AI will remain as the key market engine into 2027
data.description:
HSBC sees artificial intelligence as the dominant force shaping markets in 2027, with adoption set to accelerate as models become more powerful. The bank expects this shift to deliver measurable productivity gains and spark a wider wave of innovation across industries.

It argues that the recent drop in IT price-to-earnings ratios to five-year lows signals excessive caution about near-term AI monetization and an undue focus on short-term results. Attention instead centers on the opportunities likely to emerge over the next six to twelve months. 

HSBC noted that adoption remains early. The average U.S. company currently spends only $16 per employee each month on AI, leaving considerable room for expansion. Productivity improvements should pick up further in 2027 for three reasons: models continue to grow more capable, costs per token keep falling, and usage moves beyond chatbots toward AI agents and physical AI applications. 

On this basis, HSBC holds a risk-on stance, viewing sustained AI deployment as a source of real economic gains that should continue to support market performance.

data.title: 4 stocks to watch on Friday: NVDA, ANT, UBER, and MU
data.description:
Stock index futures surged on Friday as Wall Street looked to close out a volatile week with a winning session, while Treasury yields moved higher following the Thanksgiving holiday break.

Here are four stocks to watch on the day:

Nvidia (NVDA) shares rose 4% in premarket trading Friday, ahead of a shortened trading session, although the gains offered little evidence that the chipmaker had put a volatile week behind it. The stock surged 31% on Monday following Jensen Huang’s dramatic return as chief executive and president, but subsequently surrendered some of those gains, falling 5.9% on Tuesday and closing 3.91% lower on Wednesday after dropping as much as 7% during the session.

Anthropic (ANT) shares rose 3.3% in premarket trading Friday as the newly listed company looked to recover from a rocky start on the public markets. The stock snapped a three-session losing streak on Wednesday, gaining 1.08% ahead of the Thanksgiving break, but its losses over the first five trading sessions had pushed it to $82.79, below its $83 IPO price. Anthropic opened at $111.50 and reached an intraday high of $115.10 during its Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19.

Uber Technologies (UBER) shares gained 1.36% in early trading after the company announced the final results of its voluntary public takeover offer for the remaining registered shares of Delivery Hero SE through its indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, Uber International Technologies II Corporation. Uber secured approximately 87.13% of Delivery Hero’s total share capital by the end of the additional acceptance period on November 24, 2026, with the transaction closing anticipated in the second half of 2027.

Micron Technology (MU) shares climbed 6.07% in premarket trading Friday, while SK Hynix and Samsung also drew attention after GF Securities lowered its 2027 dynamic random-access memory price forecasts amid order reductions from China. The firm now expects contract prices to rise 6%, 3%, 0%, and 0% across the four quarters of 2027, down from previous estimates of 10%, 7%, 5%, and 3%, citing TrendForce data pointing to weaker demand from Chinese cloud service providers.

data.title: Chip stocks rebound to cap a volatile week
data.description:
Chip and AI stocks gained on before the bell ahead of a shortened trading session Friday.

Nvidia (NVDA) shares were up 2.4%, looking to close out a volatile week with a winning session. The stock has swung sharply over the past three sessions that included a record-breaking 31% surge on Monday, followed by two straight sessions of losses in which stock shed roughly 10% value. 

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) gained more than 4%; the stock has lost roughly 11% so far this week. 

Broadcom (AVGO), Amkor (AMKR), Applied Materials (AMAT), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM), Intel (INTC), KLA (KLAC), and GlobalFoundries (GFS) were also down between 3% and 6%.

AI infrastructure stocks rebounded too, with Nebius (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), and IREN (IREN) gaining between 5% and 8%. The stocks have been in focus following media reports that Nvidia chip sellers are warning neocloud providers they could lose access to chips if they rent computing capacity to Chinese companies.

Among memory stocks, Sandisk (SNDK) gained the most, trading more than 9% higher. Micron (MU), Western Digital (WDC), SK Hynix's U.S.-listed shares (SKHY), and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) all gained between 5% and 8%. 

Optical technology stocks, which provide equipment for moving data through AI data centers, also traded higher. Corning (GLW), Lumentum (LITE), Coherent (COHR), and Ciena (CIEN) gained between 5% and 7%.

Hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), and Meta (META) gained between 2% and 5%.

data.title: European luxury braces for another bumpy and uneven year—J.P. Morgan
data.description:
The European luxury space could face another challenging year, says J.P. Morgan analysts Chiara Battistini and Wendy Liu, as consumer spending is still resilient but discriminating.

This will be especially notable in China, where high net worth individuals will continue to spend while "aspirational customers" will shift their share of wallet towards brands with sharp, authentic execution.

The analysts see jewelry and ready-to-wear remaining as bright spots, while luxury goods will experience a “bumpy” year as demand will be driven by brand strength.

Against this backdrop, their stock picking remains selective, calling out Richemont (CFRHF) (CFRUY) as a top pick in luxury.

Battistini and Liu remain Overweight on Brunello Cucinelli (BCUCF) (BCUCY), Zegna Group (ZGN), and Moncler (MONRF) (MONRY).

Swatch (SWGAY)(SWGAF) (SWGNF) and Pandora (PNDZF) (PNDRY) (upgraded to Overweight) are both placed on J.P. Morgan’s Positive Catalyst Watch with Pandora buoyed by declining silver prices and signs of better brand momentum.

Kering (PPRUF) (PPRUY) retains its Underweight rating as the “most challenging story in leather goods,” given that the Gucci revamp is expected to take longer than hoped and will likely delay a return to growth to the second half of next year.

In sporting goods, Puma (PMMAF) was downgraded to Underweight and adidas (ADDYY) (ADDDF) to Neutral amid sector headwinds. 

Lastly, the analysts remain cautious towards both LVMH Moet Hennessy-Louis Vuitton (LVMHF) (LVMUY) and Hermès (HESAY) (HESAF) with both lacking an imminent catalyst for re-rating.
